decisions.reason: F1 explicitly invokes the actual Whitney proof, not its approximation conclusion. In thm-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps, Proof 1.1 chooses the proper finite-dimensional embedding; 2.1–5.1 construct an injective normal-addition neighborhood; 6.1 defines the smooth retraction R fixing the embedded target. These auxiliary conclusions are locally proved under countable choice, covered by the assigned AC assumption. Applied to the open manifold O, they give precisely j and R used in 1.1–2.1. The cubic polynomial interpolation independently prescribes values and tangent derivatives at two distinct circle points; dR surjectivity gives the stated jet evaluations. The 2D nonimmersion and 3D same-time double-point sources have codimension d>=4 targets, hence empty transverse inverse images. The 3D loop-representative, van Kampen surjection, protected-collar push, SO(2) framing correction and full-thickening extension preserve the stated scope. No unsupported embedding or retraction conclusion is assumed.

F3 invokes the explicit curve family, which the circle supplier actually constructs in Proof 2.1 and applies in dimension three in 3.2; it does not invoke the separate d>=4 homotopy-to-isotopy statement. The value evaluation is submersive, so transversality moves the one-dimensional attaching circle off each codimension-two belt core with arbitrarily small parameters z. For an initially embedded circle c, the path c_(uz), 0<=u<=1, stays C1-close to c uniformly; compact embedding openness, proved in supplier 3.1, makes every slice embedded. Stationary reparametrization fixes parameter ends. Apply the same formula on a sufficiently small compact attaching tube T(t,v): j^(-1)R(jT(t,v)+u sum z_(nu,alpha) P_nu(e(t)) e_alpha). It remains an embedding for all u by the same compact C1 argument, and restricts to the core path. Shrink the final tube off the belt cores and use the separately cited compact-source-with-boundary extension. Thus this is a framed attaching isotopy, not merely replacement by a homotopic knot. The subsequent monotone radial push preserves the outgoing comparison and external collars.
